A poll of thousands of 9to5Mac readers shows that Apple's price increases are likely to slow down the upgrade cycle, even for its most enthusiastic customers.

"Reduce upgrade frequency" was the most common response from readers, far exceeding other options; only 9% of respondents said price hikes would not affect their purchasing behaviour……

As we've noted before, some price hikes have exceeded 50%, with memory and storage upgrades in some cases doubling in price — all signs suggest this situation is unlikely to improve in the short term.

If you had to guess who's most likely to bite the bullet and continue buying Apple products at the same frequency, you might assume it's 9to5Mac readers, but a survey published on Friday shows that even this group has its limits.

Over 90% of readers said they would change their purchasing behaviour in response to the price hikes, with more than one-third saying they would upgrade less frequently.

  • Reduce upgrade frequency: 38%
  • Wait for discounts and promotions: 14%
  • Abandon one or more Apple products: 12%
  • Buy a lower-end model: 9%
  • No impact: 9%

Some readers left comments:

Of course, new features could change everyone's mind at any time, but this result is at least cause for hope: Apple may see a slowdown in sales and may accordingly implement some form of price reductions to maintain demand.
